articles.headline: Jalen Brunson: Knicks' sputtering offense 'falls on my shoulders' amid 0-3 start
articles.description: The Knicks lost their third straight game Sunday against the Magic, becoming the first defending champion to open a season 0-3 since the 2011-12 Mavs. "Everything falls on my shoulders," Jalen Brunson said in reference to the team's sputtering offense.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ブランソン：0勝3敗のスタートの中、ニックスの不調な攻撃は「自分の責任だ」
articles.descriptionJa: ニックスは日曜日のマジック戦で3連敗を喫し、2011-12シーズンのマーベリックス以来、開幕3連敗となった前年度王者となった。「すべては自分の肩にかかっている」と、ブランソンはチームの停滞する攻撃について語った。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Jalen Brunson has repeatedly said the opening weeks of the season would be telling for the defending champion New York Knicks, and so far, the returns have left much to be desired.

The Knicks remain winless after a third straight defeat, this one at the hands of the Orlando Magic on Sunday at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks blew a 10-point lead with 9:20 left, allowing 40 fourth-quarter points in a 111-102 loss.

The last time a defending champion had three losses to open a campaign was in 2011-12, when the Dallas Mavericks had to wait until their fourth game before registering a win.

"Everything falls on my shoulders," Brunson said in reference to the Knicks' potent offense sputtering in the opening days. "I just got to be a better leader when it comes to that, when it comes to our guys are ready to go in the right spots. There's a lot of other little things, but it's organization on my part."

Brunson led the Knicks with 28 points but was 12-of-28 from the field and missed six of his seven 3-point attempts.

The Knicks struggled from long range in their first two games and shot 9-for-38 (23.7%) from 3 on Sunday, unable to keep pace when the Magic made a fourth-quarter charge. Orlando forward Franz Wagner, taking on more responsibility with Paolo Banchero sidelined multiple weeks, scored 21 of his 23 points in the fourth and finished with 13 rebounds and nine assists.

"One thing I said throughout the entire training camp, and honestly to this day, is we're going to see who we are within the first couple weeks of the season," Brunson said. "So, we're hitting adversity now. How are we going to respond?"

Brunson and coach Mike Brown agreed on the little things hurting the Knicks. They began Sunday's contest with a 12-0 advantage but found themselves leading by just four points at halftime.

It has been a theme of sorts: The Knicks have shown flashes of the dominant playoff team they were last spring in games against Philadelphia, Boston and Orlando -- three squads with playoff aspirations -- but haven't sustained it beyond small stretches.

"Everyone can say it's early in the season; we can use that as an excuse," Brunson said. "When we get those runs, we start to look like the team that we've been in the past. We get a little comfortable, so we got to continue to put our foot on the gas."

It has shown in the numbers so far: The Knicks entered the day 29th in offensive efficiency, and Sunday's outing seemed to match up with that. 

"Games like this will tell us, our crap stinks. It does," Brown said. "And we're the only ones who can do anything about it. There's no light switch we can just turn on and go and win the ballgame. Nobody's giving us anything, so we have to be better with the little things until we start shooting the ball."

articles.headline: LeBron James hopeful 76ers won't need him to start at center often
articles.description: LeBron James started at center for the short-handed 76ers on Sunday vs. the Pistons, a role he hopes he won't have to occupy much this season.
articles.headlineJa: レブロン・ジェームズ、76ersでセンター先発が頻繁にないことを期待
articles.descriptionJa: レブロン・ジェームズは、人員不足の76ersで日曜日のピストンズ戦にセンターとして先発したが、今シーズンこの役割を担うことが少ないことを願っている。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- With 76ers center Joel Embiid out because of right foot plantar fasciitis management and the Sixers' frontcourt already thin, LeBron James started at center for the 15th time in his 24-year career Sunday against the Detroit Pistons. 

The 6-foot-9 James, who turns 42 in December, matched up with Pistons big man Paul Reed for much of the game, and finished with 18 points, five assists and two rebounds as the 76ers lost 106-93 for their first defeat of the season.

It was James' first time starting at center in five seasons; the previous 14 instances occurred in the 2021-22 season with the Lakers. In three games this season -- James sat out the Sixers' win over the Bucks to manage sciatica -- head coach Nick Nurse has used James regularly in spurts at center when the Sixers have gone to small-ball lineups.

Nevertheless, James doesn't believe him starting at center is something that the Sixers will need moving forward -- or want.

 

"Well, s--- we got an MVP over there. I'm not here to have a sustainable role at the 5," James said. "You got Joel Embiid on the team. ... If I was to say I was signed here to have a sustainable role at the 5, I don't think none of us would actually want that. I can do it, but... we have [Embiid]."​

The Sixers are incredibly thin in the frontcourt. On Sunday, they were without Embiid and three other big men who were sidelined because of injuries: Jabari Walker (knee), Dominick Barlow (back), and Tacko Fall (quad).

"We've only got about three guys left that can possibly play the 5," Nurse said pregame.

VJ Edgecombe -- the Sixers' best rebounding guard -- was also out because of an abdominal contusion. Adem Bona was the only true center available Sunday for the Sixers and played a season-high 25 minutes, grabbing 13 rebounds (five on offense) and scoring six points.

"I thought he was amazing tonight: his energy, his effort," James said. "For us, who weren't rebounding well, he came in and gave us that spark on the rebounding offensively and defensively. So, I think his energy and his effort are going to be great for our team throughout the whole season."

The Sixers' frontcourt injuries have played a part in their struggles rebounding. Opponents have outrebounded Philly in each game this season, including losing the rebounding battle by 22 on Saturday against Milwaukee and 17 on Sunday against Detroit.

For guard Tyrese Maxey, the fix is simple.

"Some of our tall guys come back. That would be great," he said.

articles.headline: Week 7 winners and losers: Pollard, Burrow lead the way; Walker III, Purdy struggle
articles.description: Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers came up big in Week 7, while Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III all had quiet days.
articles.headlineJa: 第7週の勝者と敗者：ポラードとバロウが牽引、ウォーカー3世とパーディは苦戦
articles.descriptionJa: 第7週ではトニー・ポラード、ジョー・バロウ、ゼイ・フラワーズが大活躍した一方、ブロック・パーディ、デリック・ヘンリー、ケネス・ウォーカー3世は低調な結果に終わった。
articles.body:
Week 7 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured big games by Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III all had very quiet days.

So, who were the big winners and losers around the league during the seventh week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Michael F. Florio offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 7

1. Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Pollard might be the player of the week, turning 25 carries into 129 yards and three touchdowns. He had scored two touchdowns in his previous 10 games combined. He recorded a season high in yards and totaled his third most in a game as a Titan. He also caught all three of his targets for 26 yards and finished with 36.5 fantasy points. Pollard has averaged 19 touches per game since Week 2, which has him in play weekly as an RB2 or flex option. He is a volume play against a vastly improved Bengals rush defense next week. -- Florio

2. Joe Burrow, QB; Tee Higgins, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Burrow scored a season-high 28.88 points in Sunday's win over the Ravens, throwing for 292 yards and four touchdowns. After a slow start to the year, Burrow has scored 22 or more points in four straight games, with three or more touchdowns in three of his past four. Higgins' 26.8 points were also a season high (he caught 6 of 7 targets for 148 yards and a touchdown), which gives him 21 or more points in three of his past four games. With Burrow's recent level of play, managers can view him as a top-five QB for Week 8, while Higgins moves up the WR2 ranks. -- Bowen

3. Zay Flowers, WR, Baltimore Ravens

With backup quarterback Tyler Huntley getting another start, Flowers produced a season-best 27.7 points in the loss to the Bengals. Flowers caught 8 of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown, and he has posted 25 or more points in three of six games played. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) potentially returning next week in a positive matchup versus the Bills' defense, Flowers will be in my WR1 rankings. -- Bowen

4. Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Judkins scored a season-high 23.4 points in Sunday's win over the Titans, rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries, plus a reception for 8 yards. Yes, Judkins is a touchdown-dependent player in the lineup, but he has had two goal-to-go rushes in two of his past three games and he sees the Steelers' defense again in Week 8. Back in the Week 4 game versus Pittsburgh, Judkins scored 21.6 fantasy points with 96 total yards and a touchdown on 23 touches. He should be locked in as a RB2 next week. -- Bowen

5. Jameson Williams, WR, Detroit Lions

articles.headline: Seahawks troll Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce to top NFL Week 7's petty posts
articles.description: The Seattle Seahawks' petty post at Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs' Travis Kelce leads the way for NFL's Week 7 trolls.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスがテイラー・スウィフトとトラビス・ケルシーを煽り、NFL第7週の「意地悪投稿」で話題に
articles.descriptionJa: シアトル・シーホークスによるテイラー・スウィフトとカンザスシティ・チーフスのトラビス・ケルシーへの皮肉な投稿が、NFL第7週の煽り投稿の中で注目を集めている。
articles.body:
Handing a team its first loss of the season can be enough to rattle an opponent. But that wasn't enough for the Seattle Seahawks after they beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on "Sunday Night Football."

Seattle's defense stymied Kansas City's offense, allowing just three points and 213 total yards. The Chiefs' three points are their fewest in a game started by quarterback Patrick Mahomes since Week 7 in 2021, according to ESPN Research.

The Seahawks had a Taylor Swift-themed troll after the game, posting a friendship bracelet that spelled out: "Seahawks Win." The bracelet is a reference to Swift's fans making custom bracelets during her Eras Tour. Concertgoers would then trade them with each other.

Travis Kelce attended a Swift show in July 2023 and attempted to give the pop star a bracelet with his number on it. The Chiefs tight end was unable to deliver it, but the two ended up starting their relationship two months later. They wed in July of this year.

Seattle knew all about the lore and decided to poke fun at Swift and Kelce. It captioned the post: "End Game," which is the name of a track from Swift's 2017 album, "reputation."

Here are the other top trolls from Week 7.

Atlanta Falcons 29, San Francisco 49ers 20

The Atlanta Falcons ended the San Francisco 49ers' undefeated season with a home victory.

Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes and the Falcons scored 13 points off four turnovers to hand the 49ers their first blemish of the year.

Afterward, Atlanta delivered a simple troll in its postgame caption. Referencing San Francisco's "Faithful to the Bay" motto, the Falcons instead wrote: "Faithful to the A," as in Atlanta.

New York Giants 27, Houston Texans 21

It required overtime, but the New York Giants escaped Houston with a big win over the Texans.

Houston seemed to have momentum after a late touchdown that forced OT. But New York's defense responded immediately, forcing a three-and-out by Houston on their first possession. After a big Cam Skattebo 42-yard rush, Devin Singletary scampered 30-yards for the game-winning touchdown.

The saying goes "everything is bigger in Texas," and New York applied it to its postgame trolling.

It first referenced Houston's "battle red" uniforms with the caption: "left them on red." The Giants also paired an image of SpongeBob SquarePants' body morphed into a Texas silhouette and captioned the post: "Wins are bigger in Texas." Even the Texas grocery store H-E-B caught a stray as the Giants put a spin on the logo by spelling out "W-I-N."

Cleveland Browns 27, Tennessee Titans 24

Another late drive from the Cleveland Browns led to another victory.

Cleveland and the Tennessee Titans were tied at 24 when the Browns got the ball back with 58 seconds left. Four plays later, Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yard field goal to win the game. The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Paris between the Saints and the Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

Later in the afternoon, the Buccaneers dominated the Panthers in QB Baker Mayfield's return, the Vikings remained undefeated and the Bengals handled business in Baltimore. 

In the evening slate, the Broncos stole a win in Arizona, and the Lions outlasted the visiting Packers in a duel. 

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Rams

Will leaning on Puka Nacua and tight ends be the Rams' offensive identity without Davante Adams? Outside of Nacua, just one Rams wide receiver had a catch: Konata Mumpfield, for 15 yards. Instead, the Rams turned to their tight ends (Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee) and their running backs (Kyren Williams and Blake Corum). It led to their highest-scoring game of the season. Most of the points came in the first half, when Los Angeles scored on four-straight possessions. The Rams will be without Adams, who injured a hamstring in Week 6, for another five to nine weeks.

Key stat to know: After fumbling on the Rams' second drive of the second half, Williams has nine lost fumbles since becoming the Rams starter in 2023. According to ESPN Research, that is the most of any running back over the span. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Raiders

Is the clock ticking on Kirk Cousins' time as a starter? Not necessarily. The Raiders have lost four straight and are below .500 for the first time this season. Sure, Cousins didn't have his best game overall. He missed open targets a fair amount of time, and his lack of mobility was noticeable. But he has not been the sole problem during his team's losing skid. He threw a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter, increasing his season total to 16. Cousins has his limitations, which are exposed when frequently blitzed, as he was Sunday. At the same time, he hasn't done anything major that's worth making a switch for No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza.

Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's seat might start feeling a bit warm. The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points for the fourth straight game. articles.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, stifling defense help Seahawks hand Chiefs first loss
articles.description: Seattle's bread and butter from its Super Bowl championship season -- Jaxon Smith-Njigba and defense -- was too much for the Chiefs.
articles.headlineJa: ジャクソン・スミス＝ニジバと強力な守備が、シーホークスによるチーフスへの初敗戦決定を後押し
articles.descriptionJa: スーパーボウル制覇シーズンの強みであったジャクソン・スミス＝ニジバとディフェンスが、チーフスにとって突破困難な壁となった。
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- The Kansas City Chiefs signed the Super Bowl MVP away from the Seattle Seahawks, but the defending champions still have the AP Offensive Player of the Year. Jaxon Smith-Njigba reminded everyone of that Sunday night.

For all the attention Kenneth Walker III received this week as he prepared to face his former team amid a scorching start to the season, Smith-Njigba was the best offensive player at Lumen Field. His 150 receiving yards plus more dominant defense from coach Mike Macdonald's unit and a good-enough performance from Sam Darnold equaled a 20-3 Seahawks win over the previously unbeaten Chiefs (5-1).

The Seahawks (4-3) snapped their two-game losing streak and picked up a game in the NFC West standings, with the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) losing earlier Sunday. Even with Darnold throwing another interception, Brian Fleury's offense took a noticeable step forward, as it totaled 410 yards and went 11-of-16 on third down.

"Our backs were against the wall," Smith-Njigba said. "How we came out here as a brotherhood and fought ... the resiliency of our team is something special, and we're going to keep going."

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Seattle Seahawks (4-3)

Trend to watch:  Macdonald's defense has now gone 36 consecutive games without allowing a 100-yard rusher, the longest such streak in the NFL. Walker looked like the toughest test the Seahawks would face since that streak began midway through the 2024 campaign. He was leading the league in rushing despite the Chiefs having already had their bye, and he had rushed for at least 117 yards in four of their five contests. Seattle held him to 36 yards on 14 carries and allowed only 213 yards overall. Darnold and Seattle's offense haven't been consistent enough to completely quiet the questions about that side of the ball, but it's clear that the Seahawks can count on their defense -- which is allowing the second-fewest points of any team -- to keep them in every game.

QB breakdown: Darnold was rolling in the first half -- completing 13 of his first 17 attempts for 178 yards and a touchdown -- until he made another mistake that he can't make. His throw on second down into traffic in the back of the end zone in the final seconds of the first half was intercepted, costing Seattle at least three points. That was Darnold's eighth pick over the past five games. Overall, though, it was a better performance for the embattled quarterback (20-of-28 for 257 yards). He got the ball out quickly -- not taking a sack after taking five in each of the previous two games -- and extended plays when he had to.

Stat to know: Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns. Per ESPN Research, he's the first player in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team's first seven games of a season. articles.headline: Ty Jerome scores 31 points to lead the Grizzlies to a 123-112 win over the Kings
articles.description: — Ty Jerome had 31 points, making all 14 of his free throw attempts, to lead the Memphis Grizzlies to a 123-112 win over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday night.
articles.headlineJa: タイ・ジェロームが31得点を挙げ、グリズリーズをキングス戦の123-112の勝利へ導く
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜夜、タイ・ジェロームがフリースロー14本すべてを成功させる31得点を記録し、メンフィス・グリズリーズをサクラメント・キングス相手の123-112の勝利へと導いた。
articles.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Ty Jerome had 31 points, making all 14 of his free throw attempts, to lead the Memphis Grizzlies to a 123-112 win over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday night.


              Jerome, coming off a 45-point performance in Memphis’ season opener, is leading the NBA in scoring at 36.5 points per game. He was limited to 15 games for the Grizzlies last season because of injuries.


              Rookie Cameron Boozer contributed 16 points and 11 rebounds, and Cedric Coward had 15 points and 11 rebounds for the Grizzlies, who opened the season 3-0. Jaylen Wells had 16 points. 


              Zach LaVine had 37 points and five assists to lead the Kings, and rookie Darius Acuff Jr. had 22 points on 9 of 23 shots from the field. Domantas Sabonis had 15 points and 15 rebounds.


              The Grizzlies built a 54-44 lead on back-to-back triples by Cam Spencer in the second quarter. Memphis led by 11 points in the second quarter and finished the first half with a 67-59 lead.


              Memphis made 7 of 14 shots beyond the arc in the second quarter and outscored Sacramento 42-31, with seven players making at least one 3-pointer in the first half. 


              The Kings fought back to tie the game 106-106 on a three-point play by Sabonis at the 5:41 mark of the final quarter. The Grizzlies responded with a three-point play by Isaiah Stewart, a basket by Coward, and a 3-pointer by Jerome to move up by eight points. 


              Zach Edey missed the game due to left ankle injury management for the Grizzlies, and Keegan Murray was sidelined with an illness. 


              Up next
              Grizzlies: At Utah on Monday night.


              Kings: At San Antonio on Tuesday night.


              ------

Oct. 23:  Caleb Williams shows he is all the way back on TNF

By Adam Rank

There is going to be a lively debate between Chicago Bears and New England Patriots fans over the next number of years as to who got the better QB in the 2024 NFL draft. And, I hate to go all youth sports dad on you, but I'm just happy that both players are doing well.

And you should, too. Caleb Williams not only entered the NFL MVP conversation Thursday night, but he's a rock-solid starter for your fantasy team moving forward as well. This Bears offense has been on fire with Williams under center. The Bears have scored 120 points in the three games he has started and finished. He is just the third quarterback in Bears history with 300-plus passing yards and a win in back-to-back games, joining Billy Wade (1962) and Sid Luckman (1947). You can forgive Bears supporters for being a little excited about Caleb.

• You might remember when people were taunting Williams for being a checkdown merchant. Well, he had eight completions of 20-plus yards against the Patriots. That is tied for the most by a quarterback in a game this season.

• Luther Burden III has 250 yards after the catch this season, the second-highest total in the league behind Drake London (255). Burden finished the game with four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. He wasn't the target leader, but Burden is the top wide receiver to trust for the Bears moving forward.

• Rome Odunze was clutch down the stretch for the Bears. Two big grabs on the final drive to set up the field goal that made it a two-score game. He also corralled the onside kick to seal the win. Great for the Bears. I'm not sure he's going to be somebody you can rely on week to week in fantasy. He's good for bye-week and injury replacement, but don't rush him into your lineups.

articles.description: Real Madrid haven't convinced this season, but José Mourinho's game plan overwhelmed Barça, and Los Blancos' 2-1 win brings them into the title race.
articles.body:
BARCELONA, Spain -- Kylian Mbappé scored twice as Real Madrid stunned Barcelona 2-1 at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday to end the Catalan side's perfect start to the season. Mbappé struck the winner in the 87th minute after good work from Jude Bellingham and Eduardo Camavinga as Madrid cut the gap between themselves and league leaders Barça to three points.

Madrid had gone into the game as underdogs given the two teams' respective starts to the campaign but silenced the home fans just before the break when Mbappé capitalized on a Gerard Martín error.

Barça fought back in the second half. Raphinha's 15th goal of the campaign drew them level from a well-worked corner in the 61st minute, and from there they pushed for a winner.

Andriy Lunin, in for the ill Thibaut Courtois in Madrid's goal, made a fine stop from a Martín header and Lamine Yamal whisked wide from distance. However, Madrid remained a threat on the break, and they sealed all three points late on when Bellingham and Camavinga combined after Gabriel Jesus lost the ball to tee up a tap in for Mbappé.

Madrid move on to 24 points from their 10 games this season, one behind second-placed Atlético Madrid and three back from leaders Barça, whose nine-game winning streak in the league is now over. -- Sam Marsden

Mourinho blows title race wide open

José Mourinho had insisted prematch that this Clásico wouldn't deliver a verdict on whether his Madrid team can win things this season. The answer was already clear, he said, with no further proof required: "Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies."

A Clásico win isn't a trophy. There's a long way to go between now and May, but this was a huge test for Mourinho's Madrid: their biggest game yet, away from home, against the -- until the full-time whistle blew -- unbeaten LaLiga leaders. And it's a test Madrid passed, superbly.

They were competitive throughout, well organized and structured out of possession, and always dangerous on the counterattack. This was Mourinho's Madrid, the kind of team that had only shown itself in flashes this season, now fully formed.

"I think it was a great game," Mourinho said after the match. "A game at a high level, a game that the world which loves football stopped to see. And they weren't let down, with two teams that played to win.

"In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organized, focused, with a lot of courage, playing an opponent that presses you a lot. ... For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent."

Mourinho got everything right. articles.headline: Pedri says Barcelona paid for stupid mistakes in loss to Real Madrid
articles.description: Midfielder Pedri lamented stupid makes and slowness on the ball as Barcelona's perfect start to the LaLiga season was ended by Real Madrid in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.
articles.body:
Midfielder Pedri lamented stupid makes and slowness on the ball as Barcelona's perfect start to the LaLiga season was ended by Real Madrid in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.

Kylian Mbappé scored twice either side of Raphinha's equaliser in the 2-1 win for Jose Mourinho's side, including an 87th-minute goal, as Madrid halted Barça's winning streak in the league at nine games to move within three points of Hansi Flick's team at the top of the table.

"In general, we didn't play well," Pedri told DAZN. "We were not ourselves in the first half. There are a lot of things we could have done better.

"We got back on level terms in the second half, but we did not defend the second goal well -- from a transition, as well, which we knew they could do.

"But, above all, in the first half we were really slow, we lost the ball stupidly a lot and you pay for those mistakes."

Mbappé gave Madrid a first-half lead when he turned home from close range after a poor clearance from Gerard Martín, but Barça fought back after the break through Raphinha's 15th goal of the campaign.

However, with Barça pushing for a winner late on, they left space in behind which Madrid took advantage of, breaking through with Eduardo Camavinga, who teed up Mbappé for his second of the evening and his 100th goal for Los Blancos.

It completed a miserable week for Barça. After 11 consecutive victories in all competitions, they have now lost back-to-back games after also losing 4-2 at Paris Saint-Germain last Tuesday in the Champions League.

Flick refused to label the defeats a "reality check," instead saying tiredness was the reason for the losses.

"It's two defeats so of course we are not happy; we are disappointed," Flick said in the post-game news conference. "The first half was not good. The second half, after the equaliser, was better. I think also we controlled the game. We missed a little bit of luck. But they played well, they didn't give us much space.

"Also, you could see today we missed the freshness. It's about this. It's the first defeat in LaLiga. We won nine in a row [in the league]. But it happens, defeats are a part of the game."

Flick said the results against PSG and Madrid will "not create doubts" around his team, instead doubling down on the fatigue his players are suffering and a defensive injury list which includes Andreas Christensen, Jules Koundé and Eric García -- and now Xavi Espart, who was taken off in the first half of the Clásico.

"No, no [doubts], that is clear," he added. "Everyone knows the situation, that we don't play very good. But in the big games, small things are important. They decide the games.

"We played against an opponent that has huge quality. They were better against the ball than in the Clásico in previous years.

"Like I said, you saw today we missed the freshness. After these weeks, it was not easy for my players. We have to now focus again and recover well.

articles.headline: José Mourinho not satisfied with just beating Barcelona: 'Real Madrid play to win the league'
articles.description: José Mourinho said he's setting his sights even higher after Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in Sunday's Clásico, saying "Real Madrid play to win the league, not to win at Camp Nou."
articles.body:
José Mourinho said he's setting his sights even higher after Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in Sunday's Clásico, saying "Real Madrid play to win the league, not to win at Camp Nou."

Kylian Mbappé scored twice -- including a dramatic 87th-minute winner -- to give Madrid the victory in LaLiga, closing the gap between the two sides at the top of the table to just three points.

Mourinho's team have now won five games in a row in all competitions, but speaking in his post-match news conference, the coach insisted that he's not getting carried away with their form.

"This is a great win, but when we get back to work, I'm not going to let anyone have their head in the clouds," Mourinho said. "If we win today and lose at El Sardinero [away at Racing Santander next weekend]... Real Madrid don't play to win at Camp Nou, but rather to win the league. We have to keep going."

Mbappé put Madrid ahead in the 41st minute on Sunday, as defender Gerard Martín's attempted clearance rebounded off the forward and into the net.

Raphinha levelled, before Mbappé finished off a stunning Madrid counterattack late on, with substitute Eduardo Camavinga providing the assist.

"I think it was a great game," Mourinho said. "A game at a high level, a game which the world that loves football stopped to see, and they weren't let down... In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage.

"For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. The boys deserve it."

Reserve goalkeeper Andriy Lunin had to step in for Thibaut Courtois at Camp Nou, who had the flu.

"The only thing I said to Lunin before the game was: you train to play, not to be on the bench," Mourinho said. "We have the best keeper in the world, but today we weren't crying before the game because Thibaut couldn't play. The group is strong."

Mourinho confirmed captain Federico Valverde had picked up an injury early in the match, but opted to continue playing to help his teammates.

"Valverde played injured for over 40 minutes," he said. "He got injured, he wanted to carry on. He wanted to go to the limit. He gave everything on the field."

articles.headline: Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick
articles.description: Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.

United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to pile the pressure on Carrick.

It was the second damaging result in five days following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

United have now gone eight games without a win in all competitions and sit 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation places.

Sources have told ESPN that the club are looking at replacements as they consider Carrick's position.

Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann -- both currently out of work -- are among the contenders.

Former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna impressed in talks with United's hierarchy in the summer of 2024 before a decision was taken to retain Erik ten Hag.

Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would be open to talks if contacted.

United, according to sources, spent time doing due diligence on a number of coaches before deciding to hand Carrick a two-year contract in May after the 45-year-old's successful interim spell.

It's understood there's a feeling internally that the club are prepared if Carrick is relieved of his duties.

Speaking after the defeat to Bournemouth, Carrick insisted he was in the dark about his future.

"I totally understand the situation," he said. "I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal."
